name: Inversion
body: Flip the problem. Instead of asking how to succeed, ask what guarantees failure. Eliminate those. Work the negative space.
example: Instead of how do I stay motivated — ask what kills my motivation. Remove those conditions.

name: First Principles
body: Strip away assumptions until you hit bedrock truths. Rebuild from there. Borrowed frameworks are other people's first principles — not yours.
example: Questioning whether a meeting needs to exist at all, not how to run it better.

name: Slope Amplifier
body: Leverage = Tension x Weight x f(slope). The slope is the multiplier. Not linear. Small improvements in trajectory compound aggressively.
example: Shifting from 2% weekly growth to 3% weekly growth becomes a 1.7x difference after 6 months.

name: Signal vs Noise Filter
body: Before acting on any signal: ask if it is signal or noise. Noise is random variation. Signal has structure, repeatability, predictive power.
example: A single off-day is noise. Three consecutive off-days in the same context is signal.

name: Somatic Validation
body: The body resolves what the mind loops on. Physical sensation is a parallel processing channel — tightness, lightness, pulse changes are data.
example: Chest tightness when reviewing a decision already framed as yes — the body knows something the mind has not caught.

name: Horizontal Contamination
body: Borrow methods from adjacent domains. A solution in ecology may solve a systems design problem. Cross-domain transfer is high-leverage.
example: Using supply chain thinking to redesign a writing workflow.
